core.title: Smoke-test every exposed journey router action through the real entrypoint
core.given: A flow router declares `entrypoint.exposed: true`, which requires at least one journey router action (the user-facing route surface)
core.when: Any such exposed action exists (e.g. added, edited, or flagged by the coverage check)
core.then: Each exposed action MUST have an e2e smoke test, located where the stack keeps its e2e tests (profile: e2e test location), that drives it through the real entrypoint -> journey router -> FlowRouterRunner -> FlowRunner path.
prefer: Call the real action endpoint; assert the journey router chose the flow router (FlowRouterRunner) path, not a direct user/system flow.
Assert FlowRouterRunner resolved a route, FlowRunner ran the selected user/system flow, and the trace records flow-routerId/routeId/selectedUserSystemFlowId.
If the flow router is genuinely internal, set `entrypoint.exposed: false` with a reason; it leaves scope.
avoid: Bypassing the real entrypoint/journey router or invoking a user/system flow directly.
Merely naming the action, journey router and runners without asserting route, user/system flow execution and trace ids.
Flipping a user-facing action to `exposed: false` to escape coverage.
unless: `entrypoint.exposed: false` (internal-transition-only / library-only / planned-not-exposed): no journey router action, out of scope.
core.why: Exposed actions are critical user-facing routes; only an end-to-end smoke test proves the flow router path and production runners execute. Criticality comes mechanically from `entrypoint.exposed`.
evidence: For each `exposed: true` action, an e2e test exists that references the action name, a journey router reference, and both production runners (FlowRouterRunner and FlowRunner).
The smoke test hits the real endpoint and asserts flow-router-path choice, route resolution, selected-user/system-flow execution and trace fields flow-routerId/routeId/selectedUserSystemFlowId.
The stack's flow router coverage check reports no uncovered exposed action.
verification: Scope: a per-stack check parses each flow router's `entrypoint` declaration, enumerates the actions of `exposed: true` flow routers, and scans the consumer's e2e tests (the e2e test location from the profile) for coverage — a standing obligation for every exposed action, whether or not it was touched in the current change.

Enforced minimum signature per exposed action: one e2e test file referencing the action name AND a journey router reference AND both production runners, recognised via the stack's journey router and production-runner reference tokens (profile). An exposed action with a test file matching the full signature is satisfied and not flagged.
`entrypoint.exposed: true` requires at least one action; those action names are the journey router actions checked. `exposed: false` flow routers carry no action and are never flagged.

The signature check proves reference presence only, not real execution or assertions; the gap between this minimum signature and the normative end-to-end proof is covered by the rule's prefer/avoid, which forbid merely naming the path components.

Disposition: strict — the rule fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline (severity 1, disposition strict per the strict-disposition policy). Strictness applies to exposed (user-facing) actions; `exposed: false` is out of scope. The criticality signal is derived mechanically from the core `entrypoint.exposed` field, not a judgement call.

values: flow router declaration with `entrypoint.exposed: true` and `entrypoint.actions`
e2e_test (the smoke tests the check scans live in the stack's e2e test location)
exposed action without journey router smoke test

fires: Any flow router declares `entrypoint.exposed: true` with an action, and no e2e test references that action name, a journey router reference, FlowRouterRunner and FlowRunner — whether or not the action was touched in the current change.
A new action is added to an exposed flow router's `entrypoint.actions` without a matching smoke test.
An existing smoke test for an exposed action stops referencing one of the production runners (e.g. calls a user/system flow directly).
doesNotFire: A flow router with `entrypoint.exposed: false` (internal-transition-only, library-only, planned-not-exposed).
An exposed action already covered by an e2e test referencing the action, the journey router and both runners.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the stack's e2e (smoke) test files live; the coverage check scans exactly these files for each exposed action's smoke test, and the obligation places the smoke test there.
How a reference to the journey router (the dispatcher behind exposed entrypoint actions) is recognised in the stack's e2e tests — the reference tokens the enforced minimum signature accepts.

The references to the two production runners of the flow router execution path (route resolution, user/system flow execution) that an action's smoke test must contain for the enforced minimum signature.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral: `entrypoint.exposed`/`entrypoint.actions`, the journey router, FlowRouterRunner and FlowRunner, and the trace fields flow-routerId/routeId/selectedUserSystemFlowId are core ATDD domain concepts (design refs afokapu/atdd#1248, #1251) and are kept verbatim. Only four things were stack-specific: (1) the smoke-test location `e2e/**/*.ts`, moved to profile key `roles.e2e_test.path`; (2) the reference-token spellings the check matches, for which two idiom keys are proposed because the closed vocabulary has no slot for dispatcher/runner reference tokens; (3) the detector/finding ids (`bun_flow_router_coverage` family, validator ref), classified bunOnly with the check described generically in core verification; (4) the TypeScript/Bun scoping facts (activation.facts[3], doesNotFire[2]), which have no neutral equivalent since the core applies to every stack through its own realization.
